description: SDLC Wizard enforcement hooks — prompt-based (no shell access needed)

hooks.prompt:
The assistant is about to write or edit this file: $ARGUMENTS

Is the file path a test file — its basename starts with "test_"/"test-", ends with "_test"/".test", or the path includes a "/tests/", "/test/", or "/spec/" directory segment? A file is NOT a test file just because "test" or "spec" appears as a substring elsewhere in its name (for example "contest.py" or "specification_parser.ts" are NOT test files).

Respond with JSON: {"ok": true} if it IS a test file (writing/editing tests is always safe), or if this looks like an edit to an EXISTING file rather than the creation of a brand-new non-test source file. Respond with {"ok": false, "reason": "..."} only if this is clearly the creation of a brand-new, non-test implementation file.

Note: this hook can only see the current file write, not prior turns or the filesystem — it is a best-effort filename heuristic, not proof a failing test was actually run first.

The user just submitted this prompt: $ARGUMENTS

A block on this event ends the turn outright with no chance to retry, so only deny prompts that explicitly try to bypass SDLC safeguards. Does this prompt explicitly instruct skipping planning, testing, or self-review (for example: "skip the tests", "don't write a plan", "just implement it directly, don't bother testing", "ignore TDD")?

Respond with JSON: {"ok": true} if it does NOT ask to skip any safeguard — this is the normal case for almost every prompt, including ordinary code requests with no explicit plan attached. Respond with {"ok": false, "reason": "..."} only if it explicitly asks to bypass planning, testing, or review.

You are deciding whether the assistant may end its turn. Context: $ARGUMENTS

FIRST: if the input contains "stop_hook_active": true, respond {"ok": true} and stop. That flag means you already blocked this turn and are being re-invoked. Nothing has changed, so blocking again loops until the harness force-breaks it. Never block the same turn twice.

SCOPE: judge THIS TURN ONLY. You see the response text, not the tool calls, so you cannot observe what actually happened. A response that summarizes work done earlier in the session is NOT evidence this turn changed code. If the response says no code was changed this turn, accept it — the author can see its tool calls and you cannot.

BLOCK ON EXACTLY ONE THING: this turn changed code, and the response shows no attempt to test it at all — no suite run, no targeted test, no verification of any kind, and no explanation of why none was needed.

DO NOT BLOCK for any of these:
- Tests ran and some FAILED. Failing tests are information. If the response identifies them and explains them — pre-existing, unrelated, environment-blocked, known-red — that is a correct engineering outcome, not a violation. Many healthy repos have long-standing failures; demanding a fully green suite makes this hook unusable in them.
- A partial or scoped test run, when the response says why that scope was chosen.
- A suite that could not complete for infrastructure reasons (quota, network, missing service), when the response says so.
- No stated confidence level, no explicit self-review narration, or any other missing ceremony. These are worth doing and are NOT worth ending a turn over.
- Documentation, comments, config, or refactors where the response explains no test applies.
- Work that is still IN FLIGHT — a background task, review, or CI run the response says it is waiting on. Pending is not unverified. The agent cannot make a background job finish sooner, so blocking on it can only be satisfied by waiting forever or by misstating the state, and the harness re-invokes the agent when the job completes, so ending the turn abandons nothing.

You are a backstop against work that was never verified at all — not a style checker, and not a judge of test OUTCOMES you have no way to confirm. When uncertain, respond {"ok": true}.

Respond with JSON: {"ok": true}, or {"ok": false, "reason": "..."} only for the single blocking case above. The reason must name what specifically was left unverified.
